skill.name: bigquery
skill.description: Guide for using the BigQuery bq CLI to inspect schemas, count rows, list tables, and support dbt work while handling sensitive data carefully.
skill.summary: Use BigQuery CLI patterns for metadata inspection, row counts, and dbt validation.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick and temp-file findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, SQL backticks, and documented bq commands. Semantic review found high-risk organization-specific BigQuery guidance that names Monzo projects and includes workflows for sampling or exporting data. No prompt injection text or covert malware behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Organization-specific project and table names are included in a community skill.
remediation.suggestion: Replace Monzo project, dataset, and table examples with placeholders, or distribute the skill only through a private marketplace.

remediation.issue: Content-query examples rely on caution rather than an enforced authorization gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation of authorization before any non-metadata query, and default to INFORMATION_SCHEMA, COUNT, and dry-run checks.

remediation.issue: Local export examples can retain query output on disk.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid local exports for sensitive data, require user-approved paths, and document cleanup steps for temporary files.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples are easy to mistake for commands that should be run immediately.
remediation.suggestion: State that examples are templates and require user approval, credentials, and environment-specific replacements before execution.

content.user_title: Query BigQuery Safely with CLI Guidance
content.value_statement: BigQuery work can expose sensitive data or run costly queries when commands are unclear. This skill gives structured bq CLI patterns for metadata checks, row counts, and dbt validation.
actual_capabilities: Shows bq query commands with explicit project selection and Standard SQL.
Explains INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries for columns, tables, and metadata.
Provides row count and table existence checks that avoid reading row content.
Includes patterns for finding tables by name and reviewing table metadata.
Gives dbt workflow guidance for checking source schemas and debugging model issues.
limitations: Does not authenticate users or grant BigQuery permissions.
Uses organization-specific examples that may not apply outside the source environment.
Can still run costly or sensitive queries if a user executes unsafe commands.
Does not replace data governance, access review, or PII approval processes.

use_cases.title: Inspect Source Schemas
use_cases.description: Check columns, types, and table structure before changing models or reports.

use_cases.title: Verify Data Availability
use_cases.description: Confirm a table exists and review row counts before running expensive work.

use_cases.title: Debug dbt Model Inputs
use_cases.description: Compare source table metadata with expected dbt model inputs during failures.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Table Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BigQuery skill to inspect the schema for project DATA_PROJECT, dataset DATASET, and table TABLE. Only use metadata queries.

prompt_templates.title: Count Rows Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BigQuery skill to check whether DATASET.TABLE exists and count rows without returning row content.

prompt_templates.title: Find Related Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BigQuery skill to list tables in DATASET that match SEARCH_TERM. Return only table names and metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Validate dbt Source Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BigQuery skill to compare source table metadata with my dbt model expectations. Avoid content queries unless I explicitly approve them.

output_examples.input: Inspect a table schema before creating a dbt import model.
output_examples.output: A short schema review with column names, data types, nullable status, and any metadata gaps to check before modeling.

output_examples.input: Check whether a source table is safe to query.
output_examples.output: A safety-first plan that starts with table existence, row count, and metadata before any content sampling.

output_examples.input: Debug a dbt failure caused by a missing column.
output_examples.output: A focused comparison of expected fields against BigQuery metadata, plus next checks for renamed or missing columns.

best_practices: Start with INFORMATION_SCHEMA and row counts before querying table content.
Use explicit project IDs and Standard SQL for every BigQuery command.
Ask for clear authorization before accessing sensitive or customer-related data.
anti_patterns: Do not sample rows from PII, staff, security, or customer financial tables by default.
Do not export query results to local files without an approved purpose and path.
Do not use broad table searches as a substitute for access and data classification checks.

faq.question: Does this skill run BigQuery commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command patterns and guidance. Commands still require user intent, credentials, and execution by the agent or user.

faq.question: Can it access private datasets?
faq.answer: Only if the active environment already has BigQuery credentials and permissions for those datasets.

faq.question: Is it safe for PII tables?
faq.answer: Use it for metadata checks first. Do not query PII content unless policy and explicit authorization allow it.

faq.question: How does it help with dbt work?
faq.answer: It helps verify source schemas, table existence, and column metadata before or after dbt model changes.

faq.question: Can it estimate query cost?
faq.answer: It recommends dry runs for expensive queries, but the user must review BigQuery cost and governance rules.

faq.question: Should the examples be reused unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Replace example project, dataset, and table names with approved values for your environment.
